A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CurriSeg study, with readable and matchable text, equations, eleven tables and eight figures. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix despite references to one; this is a shared documentation omission, not evidence of deleted material.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments, training-overhead measurements, ablations and robustness analyses in Tables 1-11 and Figures 3-8.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations and training-dynamics analyses.

M1.justification: The curriculum-selection and anti-curriculum procedure remains unchanged: WCS, temporal sample weighting, entropy-based pixel weighting, SBFT and the training objectives are retained. The revised Figure 2 does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same camouflaged-object, polyp, transparent-object and concealed-defect tasks, plus the same weak/semi-supervised, depth, video and other dense-prediction settings. Dataset membership and degradation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables and plots, including FEDER, FSEL, RUN, curriculum alternatives and SAM adapters. New introductory citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported settings retain 352×352 inputs, the 10-epoch warm-up, Tc=60 and T=70, the same backbone configurations and the batch-size-2 overhead comparison. Supervision settings, metrics and degradation procedures also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 6-8 retain the same component and alternative-procedure ablations. Figures 4-8 retain the same sensitivity, feature-space, degradation, convergence and qualitative robustness analyses; their relocation adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions describe Figure 7 as averaged over five runs and retain its standard-deviation annotations and uncertainty display. No additional seed information, confidence-interval procedure or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1-11 and the empirical plots and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports FEDER and FEDER+ COD10K Fβ values of 0.715 and 0.736 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1-11 retain the same difficulty, weighting, entropy, filtering and loss definitions. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and no mathematical derivation or assumption is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: a first curriculum-based CECS framework, a stabilize-then-perturb training strategy, and consistent performance and robustness benefits without additional model parameters or training overhead.

C2.justification: The explanations involving texture shortcuts, structural cues, generalization and architecture compatibility remain unchanged. The new Impact Statement adds generic safety-critical validation cautions, without a new work-specific limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces 'Code will be released' with a statement that code is available and a GitHub repository link. This adds code-access information; implementation settings, hardware and training-time disclosures remain unchanged. Repository contents were not assessed.

R1.justification: Sections 1-2 add citations, including a COD survey, RIDE and restoration papers associated with a new 'prior injection' category. Some additions have unexplained topic mismatches: Hu et al. (2026), listed as an LLM-agent memory paper, is cited for medical analysis. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds acknowledgments, an equal-contribution statement and an Impact Statement, updates publication and running-header text, and makes limited introductory edits. Most scientific prose and section order are retained. Sections 3 and 3.3 introduce additional unresolved '??' references.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is lightly redrawn with Top/Bottom labels and repositioned elements. Existing experimental tables and figures move earlier so they no longer interrupt the bibliography. The same displays are retained, with limited spacing and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: V2 improves code-access documentation and separates experimental displays from the bibliography, but introduces poorly matched citations and broken method references. In particular, Section 3.3 replaces a valid Figure 2 reference with '??', while medical analysis gains an unexplained citation to an LLM-agent memory paper. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these regressions modestly weaken scholarly precision and navigation despite the access and layout gains.
